# Siren core — a flowchart edge has a form, a label, and a group to live in

## Problem

A flowchart edge is `A --> B` and nothing else. `GraphEdge` is `{ id, from, to, style }` — no line
style, no arrowhead, no label, no length. **Nine of the compatibility corpus's twenty-two
`rejected` rows are edge forms**, now the largest remaining block, and a tenth is `subgraph`.

Together they are what a real Mermaid flowchart is made of. A decision diamond — which board 5 just
delivered — is nearly useless without `A -->|yes| B` leaving it, and any diagram past a dozen nodes
groups them. These two gaps are why a genuine document still fails here even though fourteen node
shapes now draw.

## Outcome

An edge says what kind of line it is, what sits on each of its ends, how far apart it holds its
endpoints, and what it is called. And a `subgraph` groups the nodes inside it.

## Scope

- The seven arrow forms: `---`, `-.->`, `-.-`, `==>`, `===`, `--o`, `--x`, `<-->`, and the long
  forms `--->`, `---->`.
- Edge labels, both spellings: `A -->|text| B` and `A -- text --> B`.
- `subgraph title ... end`, including nesting.

## Non-goals

- **Mermaid v11's `A@{ ... }` node syntax.** Board 5's non-goal, still deferred, unrelated here.
- **`linkStyle` changes.** It already works and already addresses an edge by index; nothing about
  this board touches how a style reaches an edge.
- **Styling an edge's label separately from its line.** `color` already routes to the text half of
  an author style (board 3) and an edge had no text to put it on; this board gives it one. Whether
  `linkStyle 0 color:#f00` should now paint that label is a real question and is **out of scope
  deliberately** — it changes what an existing directive does, and it deserves its own decision
  rather than arriving as a side effect. **Record it; do not implement it.**
- **`click`, `accTitle`, the Markdown label, sequence's gaps, the class lollipop.** Untouched.

## Domain decisions

1. **An arrow token decomposes into line, two ends, and a length.** `A <-.-> B` is not a fourteenth
   arrow name; it is `line: "dotted"` with an arrow on each end. This is the third time this repo
   has made that call — `SequenceArrow { line, head }` and `ClassRelationship`'s
   `fromEnd`/`toEnd` are the same decomposition, and the class diagram already draws five endpoint
   shapes on either end of a line. Follow them rather than inventing a third vocabulary.

2. **A long arrow is structure, not decoration.** `A ----> B` puts its target further down the rank
   order in Mermaid, so it is passed to dagre as `minlen` and the drawn diagram differs. This does
   not contradict board 5's "kind matches, proportions are ours": a rank position is not a
   proportion. Drawing all lengths identically would be a **silent mis-render** by the corpus's own
   definition, and refusing long arrows would break the absolute condition — so honoring it is the
   only option the existing policies leave.

3. **Edge labels and subgraphs are ports, not new machinery.** `layoutDirectedGraph` already
   reserves dagre space for an edge label and returns its `labelAnchor`; `layoutClassDiagram` and
   `renderClassDiagramToSVG` have drawn relationship labels through it since the class board.
   `layoutDirectedGraph` already does clusters via `parentId`/`isCluster`, switched on only when one
   is declared, and class-diagram namespaces have used them since. Both halves of the hard work
   exist and are proven by another diagram kind. **Read those two before writing anything.**

4. **A cluster's id is prefixed.** `layoutClassDiagram` prefixes a namespace's cluster id
   (`namespace:${id}`) because a namespace may legitimately be named after a class. A subgraph may
   legitimately be named after a node, so it needs the same guard, and for the same reason.

5. **The marker matrix is minted per pair actually used.** Board 3 mints one arrowhead per distinct
   stroke colour so a styled edge's whole arrow takes its colour. Ends now have shapes too, so the
   key becomes (shape, colour) — and only for pairs a diagram actually draws, so a document with
   one colour and one head shape still emits one marker.

## Public interfaces

**`contracts.ts`** gains, mirroring the two precedents:

```ts
export type EdgeLine = "solid" | "dotted" | "thick";
export type EdgeEnd  = "none" | "arrow" | "circle" | "cross";
```

`GraphEdge` gains `line`, `fromEnd`, `toEnd`, `label: string | null` and a length (name it; `minLength`
is a suggestion). All required, not optional — the same empty-not-absent rule `style` and `shape`
already follow, so "a plain arrow" is one state rather than two.

`FlowchartDocument` gains subgraphs; `GraphNode` gains a parent.

## Test seams

- **`parseSiren` / `parseFlowchart`** through the source string, for every token and spelling.
- **`layoutGraph`** for `minlen`'s effect and for the label's reserved box — both are claims about
  numbers and neither is visible in the drawn path alone.
- **`render()`** for the drawn line, the markers on each end, the label at its anchor, and the
  subgraph frame.
- **The corpus**, whose ten rows move to `supported`, each asserting what is drawn.

## Verification

- Focused: `cd packages/core && npx vitest run <file>` · Suite: `pnpm -r test`
- `npx tsc --noEmit` in both packages · `pnpm -r build`
- **`pnpm --filter @siren/core probe`** — board 4's committed Mermaid probe. Its spec's decision 6
  requires Mermaid's behavior to be measured rather than remembered, and this board has more such
  questions than any before it: which end each token marks, what a label does to routing, whether a
  `direction` inside a subgraph is honored.

## Known baseline (measured 2026-09-08, at `f17bfe1` on `main`)

- **753** tests in `@siren/core` (22 files), **29** in `@siren/board`.
- `tsc --noEmit` clean in both; both build.
- Corpus: **46 supported / 22 rejected / 3 silently-wrong**. This board moves ten of the rejected.
  The three `silently-wrong` are `seq-loop`, `seq-alt-else` and `fc-text-label-whitespace` — none
  of them this board's, and they must not move.

## Execution

- **Mode**: parallel was requested. The work is **serial**: every ticket touches `parseFlowchart.ts`,
  `contracts.ts` and `renderToSVG.ts`. Saying so is more useful than manufacturing batches, and it
  has been true of every board since the second.
- **Storage**: `.scratch/siren-edges-slice/`. **Gitignored** — ticket status lives only on disk, and
  the `Ticket: siren-edges-slice/NN` trailers are the only record in git.
- **Publication**: none. **Branch**: from `main` at `f17bfe1`.

## Planning rules this board inherits

- **A ticket that changes a type must own every file that constructs *or asserts* it.** Five
  omissions of this shape across three boards, two of them where a criterion commissioned an edit
  the ownership list did not allow. `GraphEdge` and `GraphNode` both gain required fields here:
  enumerate with `tsc` on a probe edit rather than guessing.
- **Ratchet numbers are an expectation, not a quota** (board 5, ticket 01). If you find a gap, add
  the row, move the literal, and say which kind of movement it was.
- **Mermaid's behavior is measured, not remembered** (board 4, decision 6).
